claims.claim: For d=δ⁺(D)≥1, a directed cycle of length at least d+1 can be found in polynomial time; additionally, n<d+k is an immediate sound NO condition. Thus the target is completely solved for k=1.
claims.evidence: Let P=v₁…v_p be an inclusion-maximal simple directed path. Every out-neighbor of v_p lies among v₁,…,v_{p−1}. If v_i is the earliest such neighbor, the d distinct out-neighbors occupy positions among i,…,p−1, so d≤p−i. Hence v_i…v_pv_i is a directed cycle of length p−i+1≥d+1. Greedy extension and neighbor scanning are polynomial. Since every cycle has at most n vertices, n<d+k soundly implies NO. For k=1 the constructed cycle always reaches the requested threshold.
claims.search_method: Direct proof, supplemented by exhaustive checking of every loopless digraph on two through four vertices and every tested size threshold.

claims.claim: For any integer L≥2, existence of a directed cycle of length at least L is exactly equivalent to a short-leg two-way linkage, yielding an explicit O(n^L(n+m)) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: Given a qualifying L-tuple v₁,…,v_L, take a simple v_L-to-v₁ path after deleting v₂,…,v_{L−1}. Its internal vertices are disjoint from the tuple, so its union with the tuple is a simple directed cycle of length at least L. Conversely, any directed cycle of length at least L supplies L consecutive vertices, while the remaining directed segment is a return path avoiding their internal vertices. There are at most n^L tuples, and each reachability test costs O(n+m); when L>n the answer is immediately NO. Thus the stated equivalence and runtime hold.
claims.search_method: Both implications were proved directly and compared exhaustively with brute-force circumference on every loopless digraph through four vertices for every 2≤L≤n.

claims.claim: There is a polynomially checkable upper-bound certificate: if X is an independent vertex set and every arc entering X from outside X has its tail in S⊆V(D)\X, then every directed cycle has length at most n−|X|+|S|.
claims.evidence: For a directed cycle C, the predecessor of each vertex in C∩X lies outside X because X is independent, and it lies in S by the entering-arc condition. Distinct vertices of C∩X have distinct predecessors, so this gives an injection into C∩S. Consequently |C∩X|≤|C∩S|≤|S|, while |C\X|≤n−|X|. Adding these inequalities gives |C|≤n−|X|+|S|. Independence and the entering-arc condition are checkable by scanning vertex pairs and arcs.
claims.search_method: Direct predecessor-injection proof, supplemented by exhaustive enumeration of 131755 valid (digraph,X,S) certificate configurations on digraphs through four vertices.

claims.claim: For every fixed k≥4 there are 2-strong NO-instances with arbitrarily large minimum outdegree and with n≥d+k; indeed their circumference is exactly d+3.
claims.evidence: In the stated construction, vertices of Q\{x,y} have outdegree q−1, vertices of A have outdegree q, and x,y have outdegree q−1+a, so d=q−1. After deleting any vertex, a nonempty complete bidirected core remains, at least one of x,y remains, every surviving A-vertex reaches the core, and the core reaches every surviving A-vertex through x or y; hence the digraph is 2-strong. Each A-vertex on a cycle must have predecessor x or y, so a cycle uses at most two A-vertices and has length at most q+2. For distinct a₁,a₂∈A, the displayed cycle through x,a₁, all of Q\{x,y}, y,a₂ has length q+2, proving circumference q+2=d+3. Choosing a≥k−1 gives n=q+a≥d+k, while k≥4 gives d+3<d+k; letting q grow makes d arbitrarily large.
claims.witness: For arbitrary q≥3 and a≥max(2,k−1), use a complete bidirected q-vertex core Q containing x,y, an independent a-set A, all arcs A→Q, and all arcs {x,y}→A.
claims.search_method: Symbolic verification of degrees, deletion-strongness, the cycle upper bound, and a matching cycle; additionally checked exactly for all 16 parameter pairs 3≤q≤6 and 2≤a≤5.

claims.claim: The target has a polynomial-time solution on semicomplete digraphs: such an input is YES exactly when n≥d+k, and a Hamiltonian directed cycle can be constructed when YES.
claims.evidence: Here “such an input” retains the target's 2-strong hypothesis, hence the semicomplete digraph is strong. Starting from any directed cycle C, insert any outside z for which c_i→z→c_{i+1}. If z is not insertable, semicompleteness and propagation around C imply exactly one of two strict relations: every C-vertex dominates z, or z dominates every C-vertex. If no outside vertex is insertable, strongness forces both classes to be nonempty. A path from the C-dominated class to C must contain an arc u→v at its first transition into the C-dominating class. Then any cycle edge c_i→c_{i+1} can be replaced by c_i→u→v→c_{i+1}. Each step adds one or two vertices, so a Hamiltonian cycle is constructed after polynomially many scans. It has length n, making n≥d+k sufficient; the universal n-vertex upper bound makes the condition necessary.
claims.search_method: Direct proof of the no-insertion dichotomy and bridge step, plus exhaustive execution of the constructive algorithm on all 59808 semicomplete digraphs through five vertices, including 52528 strong and 19777 2-strong instances.

target_evidence: The exact target requests an f(k)n^{O(1)} algorithm for all 2-strong digraphs. The draft does not supply one: its general exact algorithm has exponent L=d+k, and its polynomial algorithm applies only to the semicomplete subclass. It nevertheless establishes material correct progress: the complete k=1 case, a general exact linkage formulation, a checkable NO-certificate, a 2-strong obstruction family, and a polynomial special-class solution. The final writeup explicitly says the general FPT problem remains unresolved and labels the result PARTIAL, so claimed_resolution is accurate and not overstated.
checks_performed: Read only the authorized source input and iteration-2 draft; used the source's exact target rather than the draft's claim list to judge coverage.
Independently proved the maximal-path guarantee and the size-based NO condition.
Proved both directions of the path-plus-return equivalence and checked its runtime dependence on L=d+k.
Proved the independent-set certificate by an injective predecessor map.
Recomputed the obstruction family's degrees, 2-strongness, exact circumference, and parameter inequalities.
Proved the semicomplete cycle-insertion dichotomy, bridge existence, termination, and size criterion.
